description:
Issue summary: NimbusDocs reported intermittent steep p95/p99 latency spikes and occasional 504 timeouts for short text-generation requests. Impact: spikes last 30-90s and cause user-facing timeouts in their web editor. Observed across dedicated pool for customer tenant. Preliminary SRE triage indicates correlation with continuous-batcher accumulation when traffic exhibits diurnal jitter and short bursts.

Full customer impact: editor autosave requests time out, affecting live collaboration. This is urgent for NimbusDocs' contract (Dedicated, SLA required).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Send a steady low-rate stream of short (<=32 token) text-generation requests from multiple connections to the customer's dedicated pool.
2) Introduce modest jitter/diurnal-style bursts (sudden +3x for ~20-40s) across tenants sharing the pool.
3) Observe batcher behavior: backlog grows, linger timers increase, and p95/p99 latencies climb sharply for short requests.
4) Repeat with KV-cache warm/cold variants — spikes more pronounced when cache warmup interleaves with backlog drains.
logs: Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serve/latency-dashboard?orgId=1&var-tenant=nimbusdocs shows p99 jump from 120ms -> 2.4s at 2026-03-10T16:23:00Z
Cloud logs (excerpt): [2026-03-10T16:23:17Z] tenant=nimbusdocs batcher_id=bch-17 backlog_size=78 linger_ms=320 exec_time_ms=2400 status=timeout
Proxy logs: multiple short connections reported 'stream closed by server' around same window.
comments: Asha Patel (Support) 2026-03-10: Customer reports repeated p99 spikes during office hours; attached Grafana screenshots and sample request IDs.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10: Triage started. Early graphing shows sawtooth backlog growth aligned with minor cross-tenant bursts. Posting initial hypothesis to #support and #infra.
SRE on-call (2026-03-11): Scoped to continuous-batcher; scheduling short experiment to reduce max_linger_ms and monitor effect. Notified NimbusDocs of temporary mitigation window.
NimbusDocs (Customer) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reduction of visible timeouts during mitigation window, but concerned about regression recurrence when mitigation reverted.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Continuous-batcher's adaptive linger growth reacts to jitter by increasing linger_ms to coalesce transient bursts; when jitter recurs, backlog accumulates and drain stalls occur causing waterfall-style latency for short requests.
Hypothesis 2: KV-cache warmup interplay: when warmup IO and batcher drain attempt to coexist, evictions and cold-kv hits amplify per-batch exec time and increase variance at tail.

Metric evidence: correlation matrix shows backlog_size and linger_ms correlate with p99 (Pearson 0.78) during windows. CPU/GPU utilization remained below thresholds, indicating latency tied to scheduling/queueing not raw compute saturation.

Experiment run 2026-03-11 02:15Z: Temporarily set continuous-batcher.max_linger_ms=50 (from 300) for tenant nimbusdocs. Observed p99 drop from ~2.4s to ~260ms within two windows. Throughput unchanged.
Reproduction note: Synthetic test with cross-tenant +3x burst reproduces waterfall effect reliably in staging with same batcher version and tenant config.
mitigations_tried: 1) Reduced max_linger_ms to 50ms for tenant during mitigation window (temporary) — immediate p99 improvement.
2) Throttled cross-tenant background bursters to smooth input — reduced backlog growth but not acceptable as long-term fix.
3) Manual KV-cache pre-warm for common prefixes — reduced variance but operationally heavy.
root_cause_summary: Adaptive linger hysteresis in continuous-batcher combined with cross-tenant diurnal jitter allowed backlog accumulation. When backlog drained, batches contained a mix of cold and warm keys causing variable per-batch execution times and waterfall tail latency for short requests. Not a pure compute saturation issue.
resolution_notes: Short-term workaround (applied 2026-03-11): Lowered continuous-batcher.max_linger_ms to 50ms for NimbusDocs dedicated pool and enabled aggressive prefix KV-cache warming during high-variance windows. Customer reported reduced timeouts.

Medium-term fix (in progress): Implement hinge in batcher control loop to cap adaptive linger growth based on backlog derivative (prevent positive feedback loops). PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/4210

Long-term: Add tenant-aware burst-smoothing at ingress to prevent transient cross-tenant spikes from driving batcher hysteresis; add KV-cache instrumentation for per-batch cold-hit ratio to influence scheduling decisions.
Rollout notes: Patch to batcher control loop will be staged in canary within prod-us-east on 2026-03-16, followed by gradual rollout to dedicated pools over 72h with increased tracing and dashboards.
postmortem_actions: 1) Create alert for backlog_size derivative crossing threshold (owner: serving-runtime) — due 2026-03-15
2) Instrument per-batch cold_kv_hit_rate metric and expose on per-tenant dashboard (owner: infra-metrics) — due 2026-03-20
3) Complete PR #4210 review and schedule canary rollout (owner: runtime-team) — due 2026-03-16
4) Follow-up meeting with NimbusDocs on 2026-03-17 to discuss acceptable default max_linger_ms and SLA expectations.
